latin: Per uolatile quod creatum est die quinta, debemus intelligere angelos mundanos qui hominibus apparent, non eos qui non apparent nisi in spiritu.
translation: By the winged creature that was created on the fifth day, we ought to understand the worldly angels who appear to human beings, not those who appear only in spirit.
translation_note: 'uolatile' ('winged/flying creature') refers to Gen. 1:20, the creation of birds on the fifth day (farmer1998:18152).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch11, from Latin at farmer1998:18078
doctrine: Farmer reads the thesis as referring to Gen. 1:20 and as implying a hierarchy of angelic powers comparable to that found in 6.7; he notes that which sefirah is meant by 'the fifth day' is unclear, cross-referencing his note on 28.8, and further cross-references 28.30 as a related thesis (farmer1998:18152).
context: Farmer cross-references 28.8, on souls descending from the third light through the fourth and fifth days (farmer1998:17645), and 6.7, on the illumination of an inferior angel by a superior one (farmer1998:12693) (farmer1998:18152).
historiography: Wirszubski transcribes the thesis in full as his 'Conclusio XXVIII' (wirszubski1989:2432).

quotations.text: Per uolatile quod creatum est die quinta, debemus intelligere angelos mundanos, qui hominibus apparent, non eos qui non apparent nisi in spiritu.

not_established: Which sefirah 'the fifth day' designates is left unresolved by Farmer himself (farmer1998:18152) and is not established further by the sources consulted.
